lines.trans: We have a disaster right now! Remember that woman I clashed with at the recycling station…
Yes, that front-building terror! Believe it or not, she turns out to be Seung-chan's direct senior at the station!
Far from clearing the road ahead for my Seung-chan, his own mother scattered ashes all over it!
And to top it off, I caused another disaster today by barking at that same senior to repark her car!
She clearly has quite a temper—what if she hazes our poor Seung-chan at work because of me?!
Wait—did you not stay up all night at the station? Why are you walking out of that front building?
A senior producer from work lives right here in the front building, and I was exhausted on the way home so briefly…
What a horrifying thing to suggest! Surely another senior lives there—some male senior producer must live there!

meanings.note: Points to a place near the listener, and in casual or brisk speech is used to call out to someone whose name you do not know. RR: geogi.

examples.trans: Hey, you there, just a moment!
How is the atmosphere there?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 오늘 내일 잡힌 방송이랑 행사 취소한 것만 열 건이야.
examples.trans: Just the broadcasts and events I canceled for today and tomorrow come to ten.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.

meanings.note: Used as emphatic interjection (글쎄).

examples.text: 글쎄 그게 무슨 또라이 같은 소리냐고! 박 군은 어딨니?
examples.trans: What kind of lunatic excuse is that?! Where is Manager Park?

meanings.note: Used as adnominal (끔찍한).

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur
meanings.note: Used with feelings, thoughts, or events (e.g. 실감이 나다, 생각이 나다).

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.
Tears suddenly came to my eyes.

meanings.en: to appear, be published, be achieved (a score/result)

examples.trans: I came outside from the house.
The exam results came out well.

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
르-irregular adjective; conjugates as 달라요 in polite present.
In its adnominal form 다른, modifies a following noun to mean 'other' or 'another'.

examples.trans: Do you have any other questions?
Our thoughts are different from each other.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

examples.text: 회사 선배님 댁이 바로 여기 앞동이라서요.

meanings.note: Usually followed by -e to mean 'because of'.

examples.trans: I was late because of the rain.
It's because of you.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.

meanings.en: to be unable to, cannot do
meanings.note: Expresses inability; follows a noun in 말 못하다 (cannot say).

examples.trans: I cannot swim.
I couldn't contact you because I was busy.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to emphasize immediate action or result.
E.g., 바로 옆 ('right next to'), 바로 그 사람 ('that very person').

examples.trans: I'll start right away now.
The cafe is right in front of the school.

meanings.note: Used as past adnominal (밤새운).

examples.text: 어디 회사에서 밤새운 거 아니었어? 왜 거기서 나와?
examples.trans: Wait—did you not stay up all night at the station? Why are you walking out of that front building?
Let us do that (pulled an all-nighter) right away.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.
I understand well (usually).
Today is a (usually) busy day.

meanings.note: Used as compound noun + locative (분리수거장에서).

examples.text: 지금 큰일 났어! 그때 왜 내가 분리수거장에서 만나서 한 판 했다던…
examples.trans: We have a disaster right now! Remember that woman I clashed with at the recycling station…
This point about at the recycling area is really important.

빼다.gloss: to take out; to remove; to exclude

meanings.en: to take out; to remove; to exclude
meanings.note: Used for removing someone from a schedule or taking something out.
Used in arithmetic.

examples.trans: Please take my name off the list.
I took the key out of my pocket.

examples.text: 이 스프레이로 물 뿌리고 신디가 깨면 까나리카노를 내밀면 돼.
examples.trans: Spray water with this bottle, and when Cindy wakes up, hand her this fish-sauce coffee.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 뿌리다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (spray and).

meanings.note: Commonly used for traffic or workplace accidents

examples.trans: A big traffic accident happened on the road.

examples.text: 조심하지 않으면 사고가 날 수 있어요.
examples.trans: If you are not careful, an accident can happen.

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

examples.trans: school senior
My senior bought me a meal.

meanings.note: Used as noun + causal copula (성격이라.).

examples.text: 제가 좀 이렇게 정리 안 된 걸 잘 못 보는 성격이라.
examples.trans: My personality is the sort that cannot stand seeing things untidy like this.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

meanings.note: Used as compound noun + object (앞길을).

meanings.note: Spontaneous exclamation of mild surprise or puzzlement when noticing something unexpected. RR: eo.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun for location.

meanings.en: what to do, how to act

examples.trans: What should we do?

meanings.en: to be how, to be in what state

examples.trans: How do you feel today?
How did the meeting turn out?

meanings.note: affectionate/informal word for mother

examples.trans: I went to the market with my mum.

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.

meanings.note: Used as verb + -지 (열어주지).

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.

examples.trans: Do you have time?

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: for a moment; briefly; a second
meanings.note: Used to soften requests or indicate a very short duration.

examples.trans: Do you have a moment?

meanings.note: Used as noun + object (재를).

meanings.note: Short for 자동차.

examples.trans: This is my father's car.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?

meanings.note: Determiner form of 하나, used before a noun counter.

examples.trans: one person
one hour
